notable_absence.finding: This overview page asserts one blanket role requirement for the entire API ('All calls require the Full Admin role'), but every individual endpoint page in this batch (backup-get-task-info, backup-manage-config, backup-node-threads) instead documents a per-method breakdown that ALSO admits Backup Full Admin and/or Read-Only Admin roles for read/GET operations - a strictly looser rule than the overview states. The overview is out of date relative to its own children pages, or is deliberately simplified and therefore misleading if read on its own. Flagged rather than silently reconciled, since both are directly quotable and genuinely say different things.

cross_component_finding: TWO OPEN QUESTIONS FROM ROUND 19, PARTIALLY ANSWERED. (1) Round 19 flagged 'NO EDITION GATE' as a notable_absence on backup-service.md - no page named an edition requirement for the Backup Service. This overview page is the first in the Backup Service family to say the word 'Enterprise' at all: 'Each URI, in Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition Version 7.0, must be prefixed with `/api/v1`.' But the gate is narrower than the round-19 question asked: it's a historical statement about a URI-prefixing CONVENTION at version 7.0, not a present-tense statement that the Backup Service itself requires Enterprise Edition. The open question stands: is the Backup Service Enterprise-only? This page doesn't resolve it, it just gets closer without landing. (2) Round 19 also flagged that backup-service.md never linked its own port. This page states it directly: 'use port `8097`' - filling that specific gap, and licensing the port:8097 mint. SECOND, on the round's central question (is the Backup Service REST API the same underlying mechanism as cbbackupmgr, or a separate thing): this page's category breakdown (Cluster/Configuration/Repository/Plan/Task/Data) maps directly onto backup:repository, backup:plan, backup:backup-task and backup:archive - concepts already promoted or extraction-layer from cbbackupmgr's own reference pages (round 11/19) - with no new object types introduced at the API-surface level. Every endpoint documented under this API operates on the SAME repository/plan/task/archive vocabulary the CLI reference uses; the REST API is a second access surface onto identical underlying state, not a parallel ontology. This is the strongest confirmation yet of round 11's already-promoted finding on backup:repository, and this batch's individual pages (see backup-import-repository.json, backup-trigger-merge.json) add further corroborating detail below.
